subject: Biotechnology
title: Rare Disease Diagnosis
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Rare Disease Diagnosis.

hook.text: Rare disease patients wait an average of 5 years for diagnosis — genomic sequencing cuts that to weeks.

buildup.text: There are over 7,000 rare diseases — 80% are genetic, affecting 400 million people worldwide combined.

discovery.text: Trio sequencing analyzes the patient plus both parents — finding de novo mutations that parents do not carry.

twist.text: Only 50% of rare disease patients get a diagnosis even with genome sequencing — many disease genes remain unknown.

climax.text: Matchmaker Exchange connects unsolved cases worldwide — finding other patients with the same rare mutation and phenotype.

punchline.text: Sequence the family, find the mutation — genomics ends diagnostic odysseys.

quiz.question: Why does trio sequencing improve rare disease diagnosis?
options: It sequences the genome three times for better accuracy
Comparing patient DNA to both parents reveals de novo mutations that only the patient carries
It tests three different genes simultaneously
